body:
<!-- DO NOT DELETE OR REPLACE THIS TEMPLATE or the PR will be closed.

Read our Policy on AI Generated Code and Communication at
https://docs.sympy.org/dev/contributing/ai-generated-code-policy.html.

As required in the policy do not use AI-generated text to complete the PR
description below or the PR will be closed. Follow the instructions in the
template below and keep all section headings or the PR will be closed.

The PR title above should be a short description of what was changed. Do not
include the issue number in the title. -->

#### References to other Issues or PRs

See #30844

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

The R code printer was missing a closing parenthesis when printing a For loop. Because of this, the generated R code was invalid:

```python
>>> from sympy import symbols, Range, rcode
>>> from sympy.codegen.ast import For, aug_assign
>>> x, y = symbols('x y')
>>> print(rcode(For(x, Range(0, 10, 2), [aug_assign(y, '*', x)])))
for(x in seq(from=0, to=9, by=2){
   y *= x;
}
```

The closing `)` was missing before the `{`, which caused R to report an unexpected `{` error. I added the missing parenthesis in `_print_For`, so the generated output now starts with:

```r
for(x in seq(from=0, to=9, by=2)){
```

#### Other comments

The existing `test_rcode_For` was checking for the same incorrect output, so I updated it to expect the correct output.

I don't have R installed, so I couldn't run the generated code in R. I checked the output manually instead.

Also, `y *= x;` is not valid R syntax, since R does not support `*=`, but I have left that unchanged to keep this PR focused on the missing parenthesis.

#### AI Generation Disclosure

I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) to identify this bug from the list in #30844 and help implement the change in `sympy/printing/rcode.py` (`_print_For`) and update the test in `sympy/printing/tests/test_rcode.py` (`test_rcode_For`). I reviewed the changes, checked the generated output myself, and understand what was changed.

#### Release Notes

<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
* printing
  * Fixed rcode output for For loops, which was missing a closing parenthesis and produced invalid R code.
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->

commits.author: Swayam Prajapati
commits.message:
printing: close the for( parenthesis in rcode of For loops

RCodePrinter._print_For produced `for(x in seq(...){`, which is missing
the `)` that closes `for(` and is a syntax error in R. The existing test
asserted this output and is updated.

AI-assisted: the change and test update were generated with Claude Code
(Claude Opus 5.5) and reviewed by the author.

diff:
diff --git a/sympy/printing/rcode.py b/sympy/printing/rcode.py
index 3107e6e94d5c..7f1a0bf630c2 100644
--- a/sympy/printing/rcode.py
+++ b/sympy/printing/rcode.py
@@ -254,7 +254,7 @@ def _print_For(self, expr):
         else:
             raise NotImplementedError("Only iterable currently supported is Range")
         body = self._print(expr.body)
-        return 'for({target} in seq(from={start}, to={stop}, by={step}){{\n{body}\n}}'.format(target=target, start=start,
+        return 'for({target} in seq(from={start}, to={stop}, by={step})){{\n{body}\n}}'.format(target=target, start=start,
                 stop=stop-1, step=step, body=body)
 
 
diff --git a/sympy/printing/tests/test_rcode.py b/sympy/printing/tests/test_rcode.py
index 1443cc1ecb42..dffaf26736b1 100644
--- a/sympy/printing/tests/test_rcode.py
+++ b/sympy/printing/tests/test_rcode.py
@@ -459,7 +459,7 @@ def test_rcode_Assignment():
 def test_rcode_For():
     f = For(x, Range(0, 10, 2), [aug_assign(y, '*', x)])
     sol = rcode(f)
-    assert sol == ("for(x in seq(from=0, to=9, by=2){\n"
+    assert sol == ("for(x in seq(from=0, to=9, by=2)){\n"
                    "   y *= x;\n"
                    "}")

linked.body:
> **AI disclosure.** This issue text and the underlying review were produced by an AI agent (Claude Code, models Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1) at the request of the account owner. Every finding below was executed on master `bfb177ed52` (2026-10-25); reviewer findings were re-run by an independent verification pass. Items whose target language had no compiler available here (Fortran, Rust, Octave, R, Maple, Mathematica, GLSL, torch) are marked **(R)**: the printer output was executed, the language semantics were checked against that language's documentation.

This is a systematic review of all printers for **wrong precedence** (missing parentheses that change the meaning of the printed expression) plus other defects (wrong output, invalid output, crashes on valid input, ignored settings). It is one umbrella issue so the findings can be triaged together; individual items can be split out as needed. Items marked **tested-buggy** have an existing test asserting the wrong output.

Method: code reading of every `_print_*`/`_latex`/`_pretty`/`_sympystr` method, ~5000 hand-built constructs (mostly `evaluate=False` / `UnevaluatedExpr` trees), random-tree fuzzers that evaluate the printed output numerically (Python/mpmath/NumPy via `eval`, C via gcc, JS via node, Julia 1.12) or round-trip it (`parse_expr` for str, `eval` for srepr, pdflatex for LaTeX validity).

Setup used in the reproducers:
```python
from sympy import *
x, y, z, n, k, i, j, a, b, s, t = symbols('x y z n k i j a b s t'); f, g = symbols('f g', cls=Function)
A, B = MatrixSymbol('A', 2, 2), MatrixSymbol('B', 2, 2)
P = lambda b, e: Pow(b, e, evaluate=False); M = lambda *a: Mul(*a, evaluate=False)
```


### 1. `precedence_traditional` never reaches `precedence_Mul` 
(`printing/precedence.py:145,181-183`): `PRECEDENCE_TRADITIONAL = PRECEDENCE.copy()` contains the key `"Mul"`, so the class-name lookup returns 50 for every `Mul` and never calls `precedence_Mul`, which returns Add (40) for negative Muls. `precedence_traditional(-x) == 50` but `precedence(-x) == 40`. Every LaTeX/pretty `parenthesize(..., PRECEDENCE['Mul'], strict=True)` misses negative Muls: `latex(Mod(-x,y)) == latex(-Mod(x,y)) == '- x \bmod y'`; `latex(Quaternion(x,-y,z,w))` gives `x + - y i + ...`.
### 2. `CodePrinter._print_Mul` re-evaluates denominators*; **fixed in #31103**
(`codeprinter.py:576`, `b.append(Pow(item.base, -item.exp))`): `Pow(Pow(y,-1),1)` evaluates back to `Pow(y,-1)`, which has Pow precedence but prints as `1/y`, so no parentheses are added. `M(x, P(P(y,-1),-1))` (= `parse_expr('x/(1/y)', evaluate=False)`) prints `x/1/y` in pycode, `x/1.0/y` in C/R/GLSL, `x ./ 1 ./ y` in Julia, `x./1./y` in Octave, `x/1d0/y` in Fortran, `x/1/y` in JS/Maple — wrong value in every CodePrinter subclass (Rust and Mathematica are fine). Executed in Python, C, JS, Julia.  
### 3. Relational lhs/rhs are never parenthesized in LaTeX 
(`latex.py:1721`), pretty (`pretty.py:223-229`) and most code printers (`c.py:392`, `jscode.py:129`, `julia.py:191`, `octave.py:209`, `rcode.py:238`, `rust.py:446`, `mathematica.py:166`, `glsl.py:296`, `fortran.py:376`): `ccode(Eq(x, Eq(y,z), evaluate=False))` gives `x == y == z`; `julia_code(Eq(x>1, y>1, evaluate=False))` gives `x > 1 == y > 1`, a chained comparison (executed: wrong value). See #11366.
### 4. `_print_Not` tests `arg.is_Boolean`*, which is False for `Relational` and `Contains` 
(`latex.py:1154`, `pretty.py:241`): `latex(Not(x>y, evaluate=False))` gives `\neg x > y`; `latex(Not(Contains(x, Interval(0,1))))` gives `\neg x \in \left[0, 1\right]`.
### 5. Pretty printer returns composite pictures with ATOM binding
(inline `p/q` Rationals, negative Floats, Union/`_print_seq`, MatAdd, Dot, TensorProduct, inline `sin²(x)`), so `prettyForm.__pow__`/`__mul__` add no parentheses: `pprint(P(Rational(2,3), x))` prints `2/3` with superscript `x` (reads 2/3ˣ); `Rational(-1,2)**n + x` prints `-1/2ⁿ + x`. Shows up in `fps(sin(x))`.
### 6. The Limit direction marker is glued to the printed point
(`latex.py:922`, `pretty.py:680-688`): `latex(Limit(f(x),x,a+b))` gives `\lim_{x \to a + b^+}`; `Limit(f(x),x,a**2)` gives `a^{2}^+` (TeX double-superscript error).
## LaTeX printer (`printing/latex.py` and external `_latex` methods)

<details><summary>Crashes / invalid TeX (every TeX claim confirmed with pdflatex)</summary>

- `latex(LaplaceTransform(f(t),t,s)**2)` → `TypeError: _print_LaplaceTransform() got an unexpected keyword argument 'exp'`. Same for all Mellin/Fourier/Sine/Cosine transforms and inverses, `Pow(Piecewise(...),2,evaluate=False)`, `Lambda(x,x**2)**2`, and any Function subclass with `_latex(self, printer)` (e.g. the biomechanics curves, user Functions). `latex.py:686,714` pass `exp=` for every `is_Function` base.
- `latex(Feedback(Series(t1,t2), t3))` prints a Python tuple in the denominator (`\left( \frac{1}{1}, \ ...\right)`): stray comma at `latex.py:2769`, `den_term_2 = tf, Series(...)`.
- Double superscripts (TeX error): `Limit(f(x),x,a**2)` → `a^{2}^+`; `Operator('A^a')**2` → `A^{a}^{2}` (`parenthesize_super` only for `is_Symbol` bases, `latex.py:726`); `adjoint(Symbol('A^a', commutative=False))` → `A^{a}^{\dagger}` (`complexes.py:1023-1028`); `RaisingOp('a')**2` → `a^{\dagger}^{2}`; `Die('D^6',6)**2` → `D^{6}^{2}`; `HadamardPower(MatrixSymbol('A^b',2,2),2)` → `A^{b}^{\circ {2}}` (`latex.py:1903`); `udivisor_sigma(n)**2` → `\sigma^*^{2}\left(n\right)` (`latex.py:3004`; **tested-buggy** `test_latex.py:789,791`); `units.degree**2` → `^\circ^{2}`; `UnevaluatedExpr(exp(z))**2` → `e^{z}^{2}` (the `is_Function` branch is skipped and `precedence_traditional` unwraps UnevaluatedExpr to Func precedence).
- `AntiSymmetricTensor('v_1',(i,),(j,))` → `{v_1^{i}_{j}}` (double subscript; `secondquant.py:218`).
- `latex(Array(list(range(24)),(2,12)))` → `\begin{array}{cc}` with 12 columns ("Extra alignment tab"): `latex.py:1970` uses `shape[0]` instead of `shape[-1]`. This is the fix for #26652 and fails on that issue's own reproducer `Array(ones(2,11))`.
- `latex(Array([]))`, `Array([],(0,2))`, `Array([],(2,0))` → `IndexError` (`latex.py:2001`); pretty crashes too (`pretty.py:1301`).
- `latex(Permutation(list(range(1,12))+[0]), perm_cyclic=False)` → `pmatrix` with 12 columns (amsmath max 10; `latex.py:465`).
- Units: `Quantity._latex` wraps the abbreviation in `\text{}` unescaped: `latex(josephson_constant)` → `\text{K_j}` ("Missing $ inserted"); same for `von_klitzing_constant`, `coulomb_constant`, `planck_energy_density`, `vacuum_permittivity`, `avogadro_number`, `magnetic_constant`, any `Quantity('foo_bar')` (`units/quantities.py:113-117`, `unit_definitions.py:293,296,312,373`). `latex(hbar)` → `\text{hbar}` (stylistic).
- diffgeom names in `\text{}` unescaped/untranslated: `Patch('P_1', M)` → `\text{P_1}_{\text{M}}`; `Manifold('alpha',2)` → `\text{\alpha}` (`latex.py:2926,2935,2938`). `CoordSys3D('C_1').x` → `\boldsymbol{x}_{\textbf{C_1}}` (`latex.py:2951`).
- `latex_escape` emits `\textbackslash`/`\textasciitilde`/`\textasciicircum` without a terminating `{}`: `latex('a\\b')` → `\mathtt{\text{a\textbackslashb}}` ("Undefined control sequence"; `latex.py:135,138,139`).
- Symbol/function names with TeX-special characters leak raw: `Symbol('a%b')+1` → `a%b + 1` (comment), likewise `#`, `&`, `$`, `{`; `latex(Function('a%b')(x))` crashes with `ValueError: unsupported format character` (`latex.py:1036`). `_print_Symbol`/`_hprint_Function` never call `latex_escape`.
- `disable_split_super_sub=True`: `Symbol('x^2')` → `x\^2` (text accent in math mode); `Function('f_1')(x)` → `\operatorname{f\}_1{\left(x \right)}` (unbalanced brace; `latex.py:954-957,1698`). The setting is missing from the `latex()` docstring.
- Undefined functions named like LaTeX commands: `Function('frac')(x)` → `\frac{\left(x \right)}` ("Missing }"); `Function('root')(x)` → `\root{...}` (`latex.py:941-942`).
- `TableForm([[1,2]], headings=[['r_1'],['c_1','c_2']]).as_latex()` puts headings in text mode (`r_1 & $1$`; `tableform.py:318-333`); `headings=[None,['c&1','c%2']]` inserts `&`/`%` raw (`tableform.py:330-345`).
- `latex(Poly(x**2+1,x).rep)` → `AttributeError: 'DMP_Python' object has no attribute 'ring'` (`latex.py:2685`; pretty has the same at `pretty.py:2762`).
- Custom `mul_symbol` is concatenated without spaces: `latex(2*x, mul_symbol=r'\star')` → `2\starx`; free-group elements likewise (`latex.py:200-213,2615-2621`).
</details>

<details><summary>Wrong precedence / wrong value</summary>

- Root cause 1: `Mod(-x,y)` and `-Mod(x,y)` both print `- x \bmod y`; `Mod(x,-y)` → `x \bmod - y`; `Mod(-x,y)*z` → `z \left(- x \bmod y\right)`. Also `_print_Mul` (`latex.py:596-598`) emits `"- " + convert(Mod)` without `_needs_mul_brackets`.
- `Mod(x, Mod(y,z))` and `Mod(Mod(x,y), z)` both print `x \bmod y \bmod z` (`latex.py:1883-1888`).
- Relationals (root cause 3): `Eq(Eq(x,y), False)` → `x = y = \text{False}`; `Eq(x, Eq(y,z), evaluate=False)` → `x = y = z`; `Eq(And(p,q), Or(p,q))` → `p \wedge q = p \vee q`.
- `Not` (root cause 4): `\neg x > y`, `\neg x \in \left[0, 1\right]`.
- `Subs(f(x),x,1)**2` → `\left. f{\left(x \right)} \right|_{\substack{ x=1 }}^{2}` (reads as evaluation between limits; Subs has Atom precedence).
- `Derivative(f(x),x)*Derivative(g(x),x)` → `\frac{d}{d x} f{\left(x \right)} \frac{d}{d x} g{\left(x \right)}` (reads as d/dx[f·g']); same for `Limit*Limit`, `Mul(Derivative, 2)`, `Mul(Limit, 2)`: `_needs_mul_brackets` (`latex.py:344-346`) covers only Integral/Product/Sum. See #18349.
- Limit point (root cause 6): `\lim_{x \to a + b^+}`, `- a^+`.
- `Sum(Mod(n,3),(n,0,10))` → `\sum_{n=0}^{10} n \bmod 3` (reads (Σn) mod 3); same for Product, Limit, Derivative, Integral (`latex.py:753,772,925` check only Add/AssocOp).
- `adjoint(Integral(A,x))` → `\int A\, dx^{\dagger}`; `adjoint(Derivative(F(x),x))` likewise (`complexes.py:1025`).
- `tensor.functions.TensorProduct(A+B, C)` → `A + B \otimes C`; diffgeom `TensorProduct`/`WedgeProduct` the same (`latex.py:2116-2122`); quantum `A*TensorProduct(A,B)` → `A {A}\otimes {B}` (TensorProduct has Mul precedence in `precedence.py:151`).
- `InnerProduct(Bra('a'),Ket('b'))**2` → `\left\langle a \right. {\left|b\right\rangle }^{2}` (squares only the ket); `OuterProduct(...)**2` likewise.
- `Pow(Float('2.5e20'),2,evaluate=False)` → `{2.5 \cdot 10^{20}}^{2}` (braces only; renders as stacked scripts). **Tested-buggy** `test_latex.py:2555`. See #21159.
- `x*AlgebraicNumber(sqrt(2),[1,2])` → `x \sqrt{2} + 2`; `Pow(AlgebraicNumber(...),2)` → `\sqrt{2} + 2^{2}`: `_print_AlgebraicNumber` (`latex.py:651-655`) prints `as_expr()` while the object is an Atom.
- `M(2, M(-y, z))` → `2 - y z`; `M(x, M(-y,z))` → `x - y z` (`_needs_mul_brackets` relies on `could_extract_minus_sign()`, which only checks `args[0].is_Number`, `latex.py:333-335`).
- `MatMul(A, -x, B)` → `A - x B`; `MatMul(A, -x)` → `A - x` (`latex.py:1847`); `MatMul(2, 3, A)` → `2 3 A` (no `\cdot`, `latex.py:1856-1858`).
- `Operator(x+y)**2` → `x + y^{2}`; `Dagger(Operator(x+y))` → `x + y^{\dagger}` (`qexpr.py:313`; Operator is Atom).
- `ConditionSet(x, Or(x>1,x<0), S.Reals)` → `x \in \mathbb{R} \wedge x > 1 \vee x < 0` (`latex.py:2442-2446`).
- `divisor_sigma(n, k+1)` → `\sigma_k + 1\left(n\right)`; `divisor_sigma(n, 10)` → `\sigma_10` (`latex.py:2989,2999`; `udivisor_sigma` same).
- `ArrayElement(ArrayAdd(A1,B1),(i,))` → `{{A + B}_{i}}` (`latex.py:2088` passes `True` as positional `is_neg` instead of `strict=True`).
- physics.vector `_latex` parenthesizes only `Add` coefficients: `UnevaluatedExpr(x+y)*N.x` → `x + y\mathbf{\hat{n}_x}`; `Mod(x,2)*N.x`, `Integral(x,x)*N.x` likewise (`vector.py:244-245`, `dyadic.py:188-190`). str has the same (`vector.py:318`, `dyadic.py:271`).
- Ring/field elements over QQ with Python ground types (no gmpy2): `field('x,y',QQ); latex(fx/(fy-1))` → `\frac{x}{y - \mathtt{\text{-1}}}`; `ring('x',QQ); latex(qx - QQ(1,2))` → `x - \mathtt{\text{-1/2}}` (no `_print_` handler for `PythonMPQ`, so `rings.py:2485-2487` never strips the sign).
- `fold_func_brackets=True`: `latex(f(x))` → `fx`; `f(2*x)` → `f2 x`; `\operatorname{asinh}x`; `\cos {- x}` (`latex.py:1029`).
- `Differential(R2_r.x)**2` → `\operatorname{d}x^{2}`.
</details>

<details><summary>Settings ignored / wrong helper / lower severity</summary>

- `decimal_separator='comma'`: the element separator is not switched to `;` outside tuple/list/set, so `Interval(1.5,2.5)` → `\left[1{,}5, 2{,}5\right]`, `f(1.5,2.5)` → `f{\left(1{,}5,2{,}5 \right)}`, `Max(x,1.5)` likewise (ambiguous).
- `fold_short_frac`/`fold_frac_powers` ignored on the Rational-base path: `P(Rational(1,2),Rational(-2,3))` → `\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})^{2/3}}` (plain `(`, slash exponent; `latex.py:695-701`).
- `adjoint_style` ignored by the `adjoint` function and hence `Dagger(Operator)` (`complexes.py:1023-1028`); only matrix `Adjoint` honours it.
- `DiagramGrid` ignores every setting (`latex.py:2853` calls module-level `latex()`).
- `str()` instead of `self._print`: `DFT(Symbol('alpha'))` → `\text{DFT}_{alpha}` (`latex.py:2808`); `TransferFunctionMatrix` of `DiscreteTransferFunction` prints raw `{0.100000000000000}`/`T_s` (`latex.py:2803-2804`).
- `inv_trig_style` ignored for function classes: `latex(asin, inv_trig_style='full')` → `\operatorname{asin}`, so `A.applyfunc(asin)` is affected (`latex.py:1063-1067`).
- `mat_symbol_style='plain'` prints `OneMatrix`/`ZeroMatrix` as bare `1`/`0`: `MatMul(A, OneMatrix(2,2))` → `A 1`.
- `ArrayAdd(A1,-B1)` → `A + -1 \boxtimes B` (no sign handling, `latex.py:2137`).
- `_hprint_Function` splits trailing digits/underscores of built-in names: `atan2(y,x)` → `\operatorname{atan}_{2}`, `erf2`, `jacobi_symbol` → `\operatorname{jacobi}_{symbol}`, codegen `exp2`/`expm1`.
- `PurePoly(x**2+1,x)` → `\operatorname{PurePoly}{\left( _0^{2} + 1, _0, ...\right)}` (empty-base scripts).
- Monospace fallbacks: `domain=\mathtt{\text{QQ<sqrt(2)>}}`, `\mathtt{\text{ZZ\_I}}`, ring elements over GF/RR/EX/algebraic fields, HolonomicFunction, DomainMatrix, PowerBasis; raw class names `SetExpr\left(...\right)`, `Operator\left(A,B\right)`, `QFT_{0,2}`, `CartanType('A2')` → `\text{TypeA}` (rank lost).
- Redundant parentheses: `MatPow(Identity(2),2)` → `\left(\mathbb{I}\right)^{2}`; sympy.vector `x*C.i` → `\left(x\right)\mathbf{\hat{i}_{C}}`; `TensMul` `x\frac{1}{y}A{}^{i}`.
- `MatrixSymbol('A^b',2,2)[0:1,0:1]` → `A^{b}\left[:1, :1\right]` (`latex.py:1800`); `exp_polar(x)` → `e^{x}` (acknowledged TODO); unevaluated `Mul(x, 3)` → `x 3`, `Mul(sin(2), 3)` → `\sin{\left(2 \right)} 3`.
</details>

## Pretty printer (`printing/pretty/`)

<details><summary>Picture reads as a different expression</summary>

- `pretty(MatAdd(B,(1-x)*A), order='none')` → `B (1 - x)⋅A` (the `+` is dropped; `pretty.py:907-913` assumes a "negative" term starts with `-`). Related **tested-buggy** spacing `"-A*B -B*C + A*B*C"` in `test_MatrixSymbol_printing`.
- A Sum/Product/Limit that is not the last factor of a Mul captures the following factors: `Product(k,(k,1,n))*Sum(1/k,(k,1,n))` puts the Sum inside the Product body; `Sum(1/k,(k,1,n))*Limit(sin(k*x)/x,x,0)` likewise (`pretty.py:2057-2126`, bindings at 555/664/691, `stringpict.py:452/459`). Evaluated expressions.
- Root cause 5: `P(Rational(2,3),x)`, `Rational(-1,2)**n + x`, `Float(-2.5)**n` lose parentheses on the base (`pretty.py:2212-2218,88-94`).

</details>

<details><summary>Rust (R; no rustc)</summary>

- Method call binds tighter than unary minus: `rust_code(P(Float(-2.5),2))` → `-2.5_f64.powi(2)` (= −6.25); `(-2)**x` → `-2.0_f64.powf(x)`; `UnevaluatedExpr(x-y)**2` → `x - y.powi(2)` (`rust.py:339` parenthesizes only when `len(args) > 1`).
- `as` casts not parenthesized (with `i, j` integer): `rust_code(Eq(x, i+j))` → `x == i + j as f64`; with `x` also real, `rust_code(x*(i+j))` → `x*i + j as f64` (`rust.py:421`). Same bug as #28418 (reopened; fix in #30867), still present for a cast of an Add.
- Crashes: `rust_code(Rational(1,2)**x)`, `sin(S.Half)` → `TypeError: _print_Rational() got an unexpected keyword argument '_type'` (`rust.py:441`); `sqrt(i)`, `i**x`, anything with `UnevaluatedExpr` → `cannot create mpf` (`rust.py:417,574`).
- Invalid literals/types: `x.ln()/2_i32.ln()`, `1_i32.atan2(x)`, `2/x` (int / f64), `i.powi(2)` (i32 has no `powi`), `Max(2,x)` → `{2} else {x}` (mismatched arm types). See #26967, #27275.
- `rust_code(Dummy('x') + Symbol('x'))` → `x + x` (`rust.py:471-472`); `codegen(..., 'Rust')`/`RustCodePrinter().doprint` bypass the `rust_code` rewrites (`// unsupported: Mod`, `max(x, y)`; see #26993); floats with 15 digits (**tested-buggy** `test_rust.py:369`).
</details>

<details><summary>Octave / R / Maple / Mathematica / GLSL / TensorFlow / PyTorch (R)</summary>

- Octave: `legendre(n, x)` returns all P_n^m, not P_n(x) (`octave.py:33`; **tested-buggy** `test_octave.py:71`); Piecewise masking `c.*a + ~c.*b` gives NaN when the inactive branch is Inf (`Piecewise((1/x, x>0), (oo, True))`; see #15012).
- R: `rcode(A[0,1])` → `A[1]` and `rcode(Matrix([x,y,z]), assign_to=B)` → `B[0] = x; ...` (0-based; **tested-buggy** `test_rcode.py:415,473`); comments use `//` (`rcode.py:111`); `aug_assign` → `x += y + z;` (invalid R; **tested-buggy** `test_rcode.py:456`); `For(i, Range(10,0,-1))` → `seq(from=10, to=-1, by=-1)`, `Range(0,0)` → `seq(from=0, to=-1, by=1)` (R error); `erf` mapped to `erf`, which base R lacks.
- Maple: `sign` should be `signum`, `gamma` should be `GAMMA` (Maple's `gamma(k)` is a Stieltjes constant), `atan2` → `arctan(y,x)`, `loggamma` → `lnGAMMA`, `polygamma` → `Psi`; `maple_code(Derivative(f(x,y),x,y))` → `ValueError: too many values to unpack` (`maple.py:249-257`); `maple_code(TribonacciConstant + x)` → KeyError (`maple.py:178-179`).
- Mathematica: `mathematica_code(Heaviside(x))` → TypeError (lambda takes one arg; `mathematica.py:118`); `DiracDelta(x, 1)` same (`:117`); `elliptic_f` → `EllipticE` (wrong function; `mathematica.py:92`); `Float('1e-20')*x` → `1.0e-20*x` (Wolfram parses as `1.0*e - 20`; no `_print_Float`); `floor`/`ceiling`/`sign`/`frac` print lowercase names (undefined); Piecewise unsupported; `UnevaluatedExpr(x)*UnevaluatedExpr(y)` → `1*x**y` (NonCommutativeMultiply).
- GLSL: `glsl_code(x**2)` → `pow(x, 2.0)` (undefined for x<0 per spec); `sinh` etc. marked unsupported.
- TensorFlow/PyTorch: `MatPow(A,-1)` → RecursionError, `MatPow(A,n)` → TypeError (`[base]*exp`; `tensorflow.py:198-200`, `pytorch.py:221-222`); torch `Transpose` of a square matrix → `torch.transpose(A).t()` (needs `dim0, dim1`; `pytorch.py:124-131`); `torch.special.gamma` does not exist (**tested-buggy** `test_torch.py:542,548`); `torch.log(2)`/`torch.sqrt(3)` on Python numbers raise; `torch_code(expr, **settings)` forwards settings to `doprint` (TypeError for every setting; `pytorch.py:296-298`).
</details>

## Relation to existing issues

- Already reported (open): #11366 (nested relationals in code printers), #23912 (pretty Mod parenthesization), #18349 (Derivative product), #28989 (Dyadic in a Tuple), #26967 / #27275 / #26993 (Rust), #27647 / #24961 (Piecewise/ITE rewrite TypeError), #19644 (srepr Poly), #15938 (srepr Function assumptions), #16464 (lambdify precision), #25360 (lambdify 'sympy'), #6520 (factorial), #12267 (Fortran sign), #15012 (Octave Piecewise NaN), #16882 (C fractions), #21159 (LaTeX Float power), #23736 (julia_code umbrella), #5520 (python()), #25271 (MathML validity).
- Closed but not fixed / regressed: #26652 (Array column spec — the fix uses the wrong axis), #4033 (lambdify Matrix with 'math' — regression), #28418 (Rust `as` cast parentheses — still wrong for a cast of an Add, e.g. `Eq(x, i+j)`; fix in #30867), #4428 (C integer division — still present for unevaluated `Mul(2, Pow(3,-1))`), #8175 (LaTeX Limit direction — now printed, but attached to the last term of the point), #11375 (pretty Mod — rhs still unparenthesized), #16536 (SciPy lowergamma — mapping added without parentheses), #24828 (cmath printer — Float recursion).
- Looks fixed and could be closed: #17909 (LaTeX Complement with Union now parenthesizes).
